transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise
From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Next: Try an ordinary evenly-distributed load to rule out load imbalance. Let me know what you find.
It's not the load, it happens every spin now, even with small loads. Gets louder as it spins faster, like a jet engine.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is drum bearings. Check how the drum moves by hand. With the machine unplugged and the door open, how does the drum feel when you turn it by hand — normal, much lighter or looser than usual, or stiff, rough or grinding?
It rumbles and grinds when I turn it. Also there's a lot of up and down clunky play when I lift the edge of the drum.

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
The checks point to the drum bearing. To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi, model ZWF81443W, off the door label. It's about 9 years old, is it worth fixing?

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
It depends on the repair cost compared with a new machine. On some washing machines the drum bearings can be replaced on their own, but on others the whole sealed tub has to be changed, which costs much more and often isn't worth it on a 9-year-old machine. The checks point to the drum bearing. I could not find a confirmed match for model ZWF81443W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
